idiom_name: one descriptor value type + one converter per credential mechanism + read-only consumption
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a value that carries a stable subject identifier plus the security-relevant attributes consumers need (roles or scopes, tenant, authentication method, assurance level), create it exactly once where verification succeeds, and treat it as read-only afterwards. All credential-format knowledge lives in that creator: each mechanism gets one converter into the descriptor, so adding OIDC, mTLS or a signed assertion leaves guards and business logic untouched. Expose the attributes through a documented, narrow interface - typed accessors or a small map with named keys - and adapt the descriptor to the platform's principal interface where a framework insists on one (Principal, IIdentity, a policy subject context). Keep provenance and validity with the attributes: who attested them and until when they may be used.
code_sketch:
# boundary: exactly one descriptor per operation
subject = descriptor_from(credential_of(request))   # one converter per mechanism
if subject is None:
    reject_unauthenticated()
# consumers read the descriptor, never the credential
if subject.has_role("reports.read") and subject.tenant == resource.tenant:
    allow()
audit.record(actor=subject.id, impersonated=subject.acting_for)
pitfalls: A descriptor that carries credentials or raw token material turns the identity abstraction into a leak.
Attributes merged without provenance let unverified input pass as authenticated.
A descriptor cached beyond verification, without expiry, keeps revoked access alive.

Wrong move: keeping the current subject in a mutable global or thread-local holder that any component may overwrite -> context leaks across requests or onto pooled worker threads, so a guard evaluates whichever caller ran last -> store one immutable descriptor per operation and clear the holder at the request boundary.

Wrong move: keying the descriptor by email or display name -> the identity provider reassigns or renames that account and a new person silently inherits the access the old identifier carried -> key by a stable immutable identifier (issuer plus subject) and keep mutable names as display attributes only.
